Header:
Date: 2026-09-01 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52m
Attendees (recorded): Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Lina Zhou (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood Onboarding), Maya Lopez (TungstenWare - Head MLOps), Noah Green (Platform Eng), Daniel Park (CTO), Sara Lim (Security), Ravi Menon (SRE)

Summary (auto):
Kickoff for TungstenWare's implementation. Focus areas: staging topology (VPC/peering), dedicated vs hosted pilot, security/compliance requirements, benchmarking plan for latency and cost, and immediate next steps for runbook and network artifacts. Some terminology mis-transcriptions noted in body.

Topics:
- Network & peering intake
- Pilot environment choices: Hosted API vs Redwood Dedicated
- Benchmarks: per-token cost and 95th percentile latency targets
- Security & auditables: SOC2, KMS, RBAC
- Rollout plan and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time. this is the implementation immersion kickoff for tungsten-ware, super excited. we'll do quick intros and then walk the runbook and network items.
[00:12] Maya (TungstenWare): yeah thanks alex, appreciate it. quick note, we have a tight window - board wants pilot in 6 weeks.
[00:18] Daniel (CTO): yep timeline is aggressive, but we prioritized inference for our chatassist product.
[00:22] Samir (Redwood CSM): great, our goal today is to align scope for the staging pilot and list the dependencies - vpc peering, credentials, and a basic benchmark.
[00:30] Noah (Platform): quick question - our current infra is mixed gcp and aws, are there any limitations to private deploys or dedicated?
[00:36] Lina (Redwood SE): good Q. Redwood Private supports VPC-based private control plane and our Dedicated pools can be region-mapped. for a mixed-cloud you can either point to a hosted endpoint for fastest path or we can do a VPC peering into the region; there's some NAT/firewall rules we need to confirm.
[00:50] Sara (Security): we will need SOC2 docs and an encryption KMS mapping, plus an audit log retention policy, 12 months minimum.
[00:58] Samir: we will send the SOC2 and network checklist after the call.
[01:05] Alex: to set expectations — pilot options: 1) Hosted API with customer-defined prompt sets, fastest to start, less isolation; 2) Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity in your cloud region, predictable throughput and SLA; 3) Private (VPC/on-prem) for full isolation but longer setup. recommend starting hosted then move to Dedicated if performance/cost need it.
[01:28] Maya: can you clarify burst behavior? We have spikey periods of traffic.
[01:32] Jordan (Onboarding): Dedicated supports burst pools but you'll need to configure autoscale policies. we'll layout suggested thresholds.
[01:39] Ravi (SRE): are there kernel/quantization constraints? we run mixed int8 quantized models.
[01:45] Lina: runtime supports quantized paths; note certain model-kernel combos need tuning. we'll include quantization recommendations in the model onboarding doc. sometimes the transcript says "K-V cask" — actually KV cache.
[01:57] Maya: perfect. on data residency, EU objects must stay in eu-central. does dedicated let us pin region?
[02:03] Alex: yes, you can pin model versions and route to eu region, we'll show routing policy config in the console demo.
[02:10] Noah: on networking, we have strict outbound egress rules. will we need to open ports to redwood or is peering enough?
[02:16] Samir: peering + private IPs is usually sufficient. we'll send a specific list: subnets, BGP ranges, and egress endpoints to whitelist for hosted fallbacks.
[02:30] Maya: timeline again — 6 weeks to pilot. what are the critical path items?
[02:35] Alex: critical path: 1) network peering & credentials; 2) sample prompt set + eval targets; 3) baseline benchmarks (latency P95 < 300ms for short chat turns, cost <= defined threshold).
[02:48] Daniel: P95 300ms seems tight, can you share typical numbers?
[02:52] Lina: for hosted small/med models P95 is often 150-250ms, depends on sequence lengths and batch. we'll run a quick set for similar seq length.
[03:02] Noah: ok we'll gather our sample traffic traces — how do you want those?
[03:07] Alex: ideal: anonymized request logs with seq length distribution and peak qps windows; upload to shared drive link we'll provide.
[03:14] Sara: on compliance — where are logs stored and who can access them?
[03:18] Samir: logs for Dedicated can be routed to your logging cluster; access is RBAC controlled via our console. we'll include audit log retention & KMS flow in the security packet.
[03:30] Maya: any gotchas you typically see during onboarding?
[03:34] Lina: folks often miss prefix caching and batching config; default batching may inflate latency for low qps. we suggest enabling prefix/KV caching for chat sessions to reduce per-token cost and latency. sometimes transcribers show "prefix K-V cask" — that's a miswrite.
[03:50] Daniel: ok good note. can we do a small smoke test with 50 concurrent users to verify latency?
[03:55] Jordan: yes, we'll template a load plan. Lina will produce the benchmark spreadsheet.
[04:00] Alex: walk through runbook — Step 1: sign access form + create read/write S3 bucket (or GCS) for model artifacts; Step 2: share VPC peering setup; Step 3: create service account + key in staging; Step 4: Redwood to provision staging model endpoint; Step 5: run benchmarks.
[04:22] Noah: service account — do you need IAM roles?
[04:25] Alex: yes minimal: storage read for artifacts, metrics push for Prometheus if you want to ingest, and a network role only for peering. we'll include an IAM snippet.
[04:36] Ravi: monitoring — can you integrate with our Datadog and our tracing pipeline?
[04:40] Lina: yes, we emit latency/cost metrics and traces via OTEL and can forward to Datadog; we'll add the tracing hooks to the runbook.
[04:48] Maya: what about failover? if eu region has an outage, can we fail to us region?
[04:52] Samir: configurable routing policies allow cross-region fallback but note data residency constraints might prevent auto-failover for regulated datasets.
[04:59] Daniel: budget question — are there unit cost calculators?
[05:02] Alex: yes, Redwood Optimize will produce cost estimates given your prompt profiles; Lina will run a cost sensitivity with different batch sizes and quantization.
[05:12] Maya: sample artifacts we expect from Redwood post-call?
[05:15] Samir: 1) network checklist + template peering doc; 2) staging runbook; 3) SOC2 & security pack; 4) benchmark spreadsheet template and an initial cost-ballpark.
[05:26] Noah: fine. for the pilot we want canary rollout strategy and rollback safeties.
[05:31] Lina: our rollout features support canary percentages, automatic rollback on latency regressions, and you can pin a fallback smaller model. will demo in console.
[05:42] Maya: any blockers from your side?
[05:44] Alex: nothing blockers — we need the network info and an OK on timeline.
[05:48] Daniel: we'll prioritize network and IAM.
[05:51] Ravi: one more: encryption keys — we use customer-managed keys in GCP. are those supported?
[05:55] Samir: yes, KMS integration is supported for Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we can support envelope encryption with customer KMS depending on the contract. we'll capture details in the security doc.
[06:05] Jordan: scheduling — propose weekly 30m check-ins during the 6-week pilot; same time slot?
[06:10] Maya: works for us.
[06:11] Alex: great — we'll schedule and include agenda template.
[06:14] [Noise/overlap; speaker split]
[06:20] Transcriber note: occasional mislabels - Speaker may be off by one.
[06:25] Alex: recap: I will share the runbook and network checklist by Friday. Lina will share benchmark template and initial guidance; Samir will share SOC2/security pack; TungstenWare to share VPC peering info and anonymized request traces.
[06:45] Maya: thanks team. looking forward.
[06:48] Daniel: thanks.
[06:50] Alex: thanks all. we'll follow up in email with links.

End of meeting.
